clue.text: See 14
Important chap reportedly avoided a disputed territory when travelling north

indicators.note: reportedly says we want the word as it sounds when spoken, not as written

parts.note: avoided a means missed a, which said aloud is close to 'mister', written MR

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: GIB is short for Gibraltar, claimed by both Britain and Spain

explanation.surface: Someone important was said to have steered clear of a contested region on a journey northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' makes 'avoided a' (missed a) sound like 'mister', abbreviated MR. 'When travelling north' turns GIB (Gibraltar) upwards into BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Big is the slang title for the boss of a criminal gang or the most powerful figure in an organisation.

clue.text: Collector's item's a bloody state, I suppose!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something rare and sought after
second meaning, playful: the state of being rare, and rare meat is bloody

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the joke: rare steak is bloody, so the condition of being rare is jokily 'a bloody state', and 'I suppose!' admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare object prized by collectors is called by the abstract noun for scarcity, which also names the quality of being underdone.

clue.text: Wet earth covering animal's lair

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece covering another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: sod is turf, a piece of earth with grass on it
a den is a wild animal's home

explanation.surface: Damp soil lies over the burrow where some creature lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden describes something soaked through, saturated with water.

clue.text: Avoiding both fringes, old Labour leader starts to eat next to Green

indicators.note: avoiding both fringes means the name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Neil Kinnock led Britain's Labour Party from 1983 to 1992

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader, steering clear of extremes on either side, begins to eat beside a Green politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Kinnock was leader of the British Labour Party; 'Avoiding both fringes' strips his K at each end to leave INNOC. 'Green' looks like the Green Party, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive and inexperienced, and someone guileless and unworldly in that way is called innocent.

clue.text: Perhaps Facebook users have seen zit burst by noon

indicators.note: a burst zit is broken apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Social media users have spotted a spot popping just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places N beside the anagram of SEENZIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Netizens are habitual users of the internet, and members of a social network are an example.

clue.text: Dangerous strain sees father and son kept apart by national government

indicators.note: two things kept apart have something placed between them, here the national letter

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tense situation in which a father and son are separated by the state's government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like tension but is a tune; the G for government is simply added at the end rather than doing any separating.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens' singing lured sailors to wreck, so the phrase means a perilously alluring appeal; strain here is a melody.

clue.text: Old men with power like propping up old royal

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces underneath prop up the one on top, so the royal comes first

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
and means with, together with
P is the physics symbol for power
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Elderly men with influence, as it were, support a historic monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, the royal cipher of King George, sits on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandpas is an informal word for grandfathers, who are usually elderly.

clue.text: Certain artists could be 14-1s by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are heard, so mail is written as its sound-alike

parts.note: post is mail and impressionists are mimics

explanation.surface: Some performers might be mistaken for painters of the Post-Impressionist school if you only listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 14-1 is POST-IMPRESSIONIST. Read POST as mail and IMPRESSIONISTS as mimics, and 'mail' said aloud gives MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Male impersonators are performers, usually women, whose stage act is portraying men, so they are artists of a particular kind.

clue.text: 1 mafioso pursues crime after kicking drug

definitions.note: 1 refers to 1-across, an impressionist in the sense of a mimic

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the mafioso goes at the end
after kicking means once the crime has given up a habit, losing the drug's letter

parts.note: robbery is a crime
E is short for ecstasy, a drug
a don is the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: A Mafia member takes up crime again once he has kicked his drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Here '1' (the cross-reference to 1-across) means an impressionist in the mimic's sense. Rob Brydon is a Welsh comedian famous for his impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh comic actor is well known for his vocal impersonations, especially in The Trip with Steve Coogan.

clue.text: 14-1's sphere about to absorb, er, everyone's sphere

indicators.note: to absorb means to take something inside
about means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a post-impressionist's field is art
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's field turns round to take in, um, the world all of us share.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' looks like a hesitation in the surface, but it supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for the Earth, the planet that is home to all humanity.

clue.text: Item worn by woman asleep next to Bond

parts.note: nigh means near, close by
a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: Sounds like a Bond girl dozing beside 007.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' with its capital suggests James Bond, but it is just a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, the garment some women wear to bed.

clue.text: See 24
Description of movement's frequently a mess if Spooner spits it out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged
frequently means at regular intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A label for an art movement often comes out garbled when the famously muddled Reverend Spooner tries to say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner looks like a hint that sounds get swapped, but here his name is just letters. 'frequently' takes MSI, the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'a mess if'; 'out' shuffles them with SPOONERSPITSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The name describes the school of Cézanne, Seurat and Gauguin, an art movement that came after Monet's circle.

clue.text: 14-1 has time for Brussels to mature with a bit of manure in plot

indicators.note: time for Brussels means the time letter stands in place of the Brussels letters

parts.note: Georges Seurat was a post-impressionist painter
Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union
to age is to mature

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An artist finds time for Brussels sprouts to ripen with a dash of muck in his vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: SEURAT with T in place of EU gives STRAT. 'Brussels' suggests sprouts in a garden, but it stands for the EU; 'plot' is a scheme, not a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ruse, much as a plot is a secret plan.

clue.text: A couple of cricket sides seen at intervals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket the field is divided into two halves either side of the batsman, and these are their names
second meaning: intermittent, now and again

explanation.surface: Two cricket teams turn up only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' looks like teams, but on and off are the two halves of a cricket field either side of the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: On-and-off describes something intermittent, happening now and again rather than continuously.

clue.text: What rice does for sushi eaters' sake?

definitions.text: What rice does for sushi eaters' sake?

parts.words: What rice does for sushi eaters' sake?
parts.note: sake, the Japanese rice wine drunk with sushi, is made by letting rice turn alcoholic through yeast action

explanation.walkthrough: 'For sushi eaters' sake' reads as 'for their benefit', but sake is the Japanese rice wine, which rice is brewed into.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake is brewed from rice that undergoes a yeast-driven chemical change turning its sugars into alcohol.

clue.text: Cycling star to turn and get off seat

indicators.note: cycling means the letters rotate, the first moving to the end

parts.note: the Sun is a star
to addle is to go bad, as milk turns

explanation.surface: A champion cyclist goes sour and climbs off the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling star' looks like a racing cyclist; it is the sun's letters cycled. Milk that turns goes off, and eggs that addle go rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle a rider is to throw them from the saddle, unseating them from their mount.

clue.text: Fickle Methuselah no longer has the hots for mimics

indicators.note: fickle means changeable, so the setter's name is rearranged
no longer has means some letters are taken out of the setter's name before it is rearranged

parts.note: H is short for hot, and two hots give two of the letter

explanation.surface: The setter, a changeable sort, has lost his passion for impressionists.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is this puzzle's setter. Take two Hs (hot, hot) out of METHUSELAH and rearrange the remaining METUSELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who emulates another copies or imitates them, just as a mimic does.

clue.text: 13 or 22 possibly taking over independent nation

indicators.note: taking over means taking inside, holding the letter within

parts.note: Cezanne and Coogan are both examples of family names

explanation.surface: A Cézanne or a Coogan takes over an independent country.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is CEZANNE and 22 is COOGAN, each an example of a surname, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a country on the north-east coast of South America, formerly Dutch Guiana.

clue.text: Jelly available in tea garden

indicators.note: available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wobbly dessert is on the menu at a tea garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to set foods and grow cultures.

clue.text: Cheat hanging around own goal area — 1 often seen with 10

indicators.note: hanging around means wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: to con is to cheat
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A footballing cheat loiters near the goalmouth after scoring into his own net.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Coogan is a comic and impressionist (1) who often appears with Rob Brydon (10), notably in the TV series The Trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The English comedian and mimic has made several travel series alongside Brydon, so the pair are frequently paired.

clue.text: Group including a precise number

indicators.note: including means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: a set is a group
EXT, short for extension, is a precise telephone number

explanation.surface: A band includes in its line-up exactly so many players.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter confirmed EXT, an extension, as the precise number. Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: a group whose name fixes exactly how many are in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is an ensemble of six performers, a set made up of exactly half a dozen members.

clue.text: Bit of fruit leading to sinful occasion's a banana skin

indicators.note: leading to means the fruit piece comes first

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit such as a cherry
the Fall is Adam and Eve's first sin in Eden

explanation.surface: A fruit stone that leads to temptation is as treacherous as a slippery peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a banana skin' is British slang for an embarrassing mishap waiting to happen, from the comic pratfall on a dropped peel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or trap, like a slippery peel lying in wait.

clue.text: 14-1's spanner regularly fixing disruption to Suez Canal when one end's blocked

definitions.note: the cross-reference is post-impressionist, and the 's links it to the rest

indicators.note: disruption to means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
regularly means every other letter of the word
one end blocked means the first letter of the canal is cut off

explanation.surface: An artist's wrench, fitted steadily, fixes the trouble on the Suez Canal while one end is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes PNE from spanner; 'when one end's blocked' cuts S from SUEZCANAL to leave UEZCANAL; 'disruption to' rearranges the lot, with PNE fixed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The French painter of Mont Sainte-Victoire was a leading figure of the movement that followed Monet's generation.

clue.text: Old 1 and silent 1 each losing a million

indicators.note: each losing means both names drop the letter

parts.note: 1 is 1-across, impressionist: Claude Monet was a leading Impressionist painter
a mime is a silent mimic
M is short for million

explanation.surface: An elderly painter and a quiet performer both lose a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' works two ways: as a painter of the Impressionist school (Monet) and as a mimic (mime). Each loses its first M, leaving ONET and IME.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, from an earlier period, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Tattooist has a change of heart relating to private area?

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a tattooist inks skin, so is an inker

explanation.surface: A tattoo artist rethinks a design for an intimate spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In INKER the middle K becomes N. The question mark admits that 'private area' is a loose sense: the inner sanctum, inner thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner describes what lies within and is kept hidden, as with someone's inner life or feelings.

clue.text: Did egg on uniform ultimately trigger meeting with my boss?

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a setter's boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: Was someone in uniform pushed to fire, then hauled before the boss?
explanation.walkthrough: 'my boss' is the setter speaking: a crossword setter answers to the puzzles editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to encourage or press them, the same as urging.

clue.text: Close temperatures keeping characters from hiking round Thailand

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other letters inside

parts.note: T is short for temperature, so two temperatures give two Ts

indicators.note: characters from means the letters of the word are taken and reshuffled
round here says the hiking letters are taken round with the Thailand letter, all in one shuffled bundle

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Tightly bonded friends in the heat keep up their walk around Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: Thailand's T goes round with the letters of hiking before they are mixed, which is all 'round' adds. 'Close' is an adjective here, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely bound together, as a close family or community is.

clue.text: See 9
